utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, if I can ask you to turn to tab 2.6, and can you tell me whether or not this is the analysis of the -- the different aspects we've referred to of killing, expulsion, detention, missing, in relation to this particular county?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Again, does the same pattern emerge in relation to the percentage of Croats affected by the conflict in that region as in the Danube region and the Osijek-Baranja county?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the pattern is the same. The percentages here, however, are somewhat higher in relation to the other counties and the overall situation in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that table, and the ERN number is 0600-3682 to 0600-3683.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will be received with exhibit number 542.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, can I now ask you to turn to tab 2.7, please? And this is a table entitled Vukovar. The ERN number is 0600-3674 to 0600-3677. When we look at this table, is this an analysis that you prepared in relation to the effects of the conflict in relation to Vukovar town?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And as with the other two counties and the Danube region as a whole, does the same pattern emerge in relation to the percentage of Croats who were -- fell victim to the different aspects of -- of the war; namely, expulsion, killing, detention and have -- having been reported missing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the pattern is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If can I ask you to turn to tab 2.8, please. Tab 2.8 is a map, and it's entitled locations of imprisonment of 2.796 persons from Vukovar. The ERN number is 0600-3704. Do you see that map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain what it represents?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: On this map, the locations have been marked where prisons and camps were located where people from Vukovar were imprisoned. They are on the territory of Serbia and on the territory of the Republic of Croatia which was occupied in the Podunavlje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And does this map represent graphically your figures in relation to -- or the locations of where people were detained in relation to the entries that you have in your table relating to Vukovar town, and that's at tab 2.7?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This relates exclusively to Vukovar town, to the 2.796 prisoners held in prison camps and prisons on the territory of two states. Of course, there were other prisons with other prisoners. This refers only to prisoners from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will received with exhibit number 543.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, if I can ask you to turn to tab 2.9, please. Now, this is ERN number 0600-3701. And it's entitled location of mass graves containing victims from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: When we use the term "mass grave," do you have a definition of when a grave would be classified as a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: In the Republic of Croatia, the criterion is three or more persons in one location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And does this -- this diagram or this map, does this relate to the figures that you have in your table on Vukovar town regarding the exhumations of people who were originally from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This shows the locations of mass graves in which people from Vukovar were found, among other victims. There are 52 graves in the entire area, but here only those graves which contained victims from Vukovar are shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in relation to graves, mass graves in the Vukovar region that relate to victims from Vukovar, is it correct from that table that there were 14 mass grave sites where victims from Vukovar were found?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that map and -- that map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With exhibit number 544, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, if we can go back to tab 2.7, please. And if we can go back to the -- to the end of your report on the Vukovar town, and it relates to the exhumation conducted at the new cemetery in Vukovar. Do you see those tables? It's on page 7 in the English. It begins with "938 exhumed and 800 identified." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Is it correct that the exhumation at the Vukovar new cemetery was the largest exhumation conducted in the Vukovar region?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In fact, it was the largest exhumation in relation to the conflict in Croatia as a whole; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And of those 800 people that have been identified, 644 are identified as being Croatian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And 358 of those people, of those identified, are classified as civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In relation to the grave at the Vukovar new cemetery, is it correct that this grave wasn't a primary grave but was a secondary grave that was dug after the -- after the fall of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. It's a secondary grave which came into existence in several ways: Clearing up the terrain; also moving other mass graves in the area; and even moving people who had been buried properly from their graves to this grave, this cemetery. The victims can therefore be divided into three basic categories. Those who were killed during the aggression on Vukovar at the time Vukovar was taken, as well as those who were killed after the occupation of Vukovar. Among them there are also prisoners of war, and we cannot even exclude the possibility that among them they may have been people who died of natural causes. Because this grave was also created by clearing up the terrain. So it's possible that people were found who had died for lack of medical assistance and who were later found and buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. From your records are you able to say what the percentage, approximately, of those bodies that were exhumed died from natural causes and ones that had died from a violent death? In approximate terms.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you percentages, but the majority died a violent death. There are documents supporting this which we received from the then Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, meaning files and protocols.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you give the date when the exhumation on the Vukovar cemetery commenced?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall it right now, but if you give me a little time I'll try to find it. I know it lasted for two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps the date is less important, but the year, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to that exhumation, you have just stated that the Serbian authorities had provided with certain documentation in relation to where these people were originally found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, where possible, you have included that information in your -- in your records?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender the tables at tab 2.7. The ERN number is 0600-3674 to 3677 in relation to the Vukovar town analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 400 -- 545, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, if I can now ask you to look at tab 2.10, please. This is ERN number 0600-3689 to 0600-3700. This relates to a number of tables which indicate other exhumations conducted in the Vukovar area that contain people that were originally from the town of Vukovar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. These are exhumations carried out on the places previously marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, in fact, the -- these tables contain 12 -- information in relation to 12 exhumation sites, and that, in conjunction with the exhumation at Ovcara which we'll speak about shortly, and the exhumation at the Vukovar new cemetery, that completes the 14 exhumation sites that you have referred to earlier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said that I would be half an hour. I think realistically it would be another 10 to 15 minutes, realistically. And so I just would ask for that. I need to briefly tender some tables in relation to Ovcara, and I'm in Your Honour's hands in as far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Press on, and it better be nearer the 10 than the 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour, I seek to tender those tables in relation to the victims listed or schooled at the different 12 exhumation sites. And that's 0600-3689 to 0600-3700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 546, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I just have a few questions for you in relation to Ovcara. The Defence counsel will have some more questions in relation to that for you. However, is it the case that your commission was involved with certainly as -- in the monitoring process and the identification of victims that were exhumed at the Ovcara grave site? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: If I could turn you to tab 3.1, please. Now, this table is listed -- entitled a list of identified persons whose remains were exhumed from the mass grave at Ovcara, and the ERN number is 0600-3684 to 0600-3688. Mr. Grujic, this list contains 192 names. By that fact, does that mean that 192 people have been identified at the Ovcara grave site?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: 200 mortal remains were exhumed from Ovcara, and out of that 192 have been identified so far. And they are on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you asked by the Office of the Prosecutor to compare these names to the annex to the indictment which contains 264 names? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And of those 192 that were identified at Ovcara, is it the case that there were two people that were not included in the indictment Annex A; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Only two people were not included in the indictment, Mihalec, Josip and Damir Simenic. They were identified in 2005, so that is the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With exhibit number 547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, if I can ask you to turn to tab 3.2, please. It's a table entitled a list of identified individuals exhumed from the Ovcara mass grave and listed in the indictment. I believe that's a mistake in the translation, and it should be in English "and not listed in the indictment."

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, looking at that table are these the two people that were in Annex A but are not listed -- sorry, are these the two people that were identified at Ovcara but not listed in Annex A to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Precisely. I just gave you their names in my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: With exhibit number 548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, if I can now ask you to turn to tab 3 .3, please. And this is a table entitled victims from Ovcara farm, and then in brackets has got "(from the Vukovar Hospital)." And the ERN number is 0600-3665 to 0600-3673. Mr. Grujic, does this table give a status as to what you know about each of the 264 people that were named in the annex to the indictment? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And is it correct to say that as 190 people in the annex to the indictment have been identified at Ovcara, that there are 74 individuals that are contained in the annex to the indictment that are not identified at Ovcara? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct. 264 names on the list, 190 have been identified, which leaves 74 persons to be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for our purposes in being able to read this chart later, is it fair to say that in relation to the circumstances column of the table, MG means mass grave, EX means exhumation, and NN means a registration number, and ID means the date of identification of the individual exhumed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And also in relation to the date of the exhumation, we have the 12th of September, 1996 as a consistent date for each of the people in the indictment that were exhumed at Ovcara. Is that an approximate date as opposed to the exact date?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This is the mean date. This is something that we introduced because the exhumation and the extraction of mortal remains was conducted by the International Criminal Court, or rather the OTP. We were there as monitors, and we don't have all the information. What we used here is the mean date. And the exhumation itself started on the 1st of September and ended on the 4th of October, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And does this comparison that you have done in relation to the Annex A to the indictment, does the conclusion, does the conclusion form that of the 74 people that are not identified at Ovcara, 16 have been found in other graves and 58 are still reported as missing? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. If you analyse the remaining 74 persons you can divide them into three basic categories. The first comprising 58 persons, and these are still listed as missing. They are still listed as missing persons. Another 14 were exhumed from other mass graves -- or, rather, 13 of them were exhumed from the new cemetery in Vukovar, and one from the Lovas mass grave. Thirdly, the mortal remains of another two persons were taken charge of from Serbia and Montenegro. Talks were held and these bodies were handed over and subsequently identified in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And if I could now ask you to turn to tab 3.4, please. And this is -- this is ERN number 0600-3661 to 0600- --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering that last document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, it will become Exhibit 549.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Tab 3.4 is 0600-3661 to 0600-3662. This is entitled a list of persons who are mentioned in the indictment and who is mortal remains were exhumed from other mass graves in the Vukovar area. In this table does this contain the circumstances as to the information you have regarding the killing of these people?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The circumstances indicated here refer to where the mortal remains were primarily found.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And this information was provided to you by the Serb authorities, is that correct, when the files were handed over?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's right. It was based on the files handed over by official representatives of what was the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at the time and now Serbia and Montenegro that we derived these elements that we based our information on, which means that our information is based on such elements as are in our possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And that relates to the 14 of the 16 people that have been found in other places in relation to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 550, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Mr. Grujic, if I can ask you to turn to tab 3.5, please. And this is ERN number 0600-3663 to 0600-3663. It's entitled list of persons from the indictment whose remains were taken over from Serbia and Montenegro. And it has two persons. Do you see that table?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that provides the information of how those people were received and the fact that they were also named in the indictment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Indeed. We see here names and surnames and other information such as where these mortal remains were buried in Serbia and Montenegro or what used to be the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. At our request these mortal remains were submitted to us, and we have documents to show that this was precisely where the mortal remains arrived from, the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to -- if we can just go back to the missing person reports in general, you provided to the Tribunal a number of the missing person reports in relation to the victims named in the indictment, the 264 victims in the indictment. Is that correct? Your office.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Before we move on, Your Honour, I've just been reminded that I should tender that last document in relation to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit number 541, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And is it the case that you have missing person reports on 262 of the 264 victims stated in the annex to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: There are two persons who have never been reported to be missing. What this phrase means is that none of their relatives ever came to us to report these persons as missing, or indeed contacted us in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And who are those two people?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Ruzica Markobasic, and I can't remember the other name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for later in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender 238 missing person questionnaires relating to the individuals appearing in the annex to the indictment. Those questionnaires and the 65 ter numbers are indicated in the second index to the binder, and I would assume probably they would need to be assigned exhibit numbers at -- during the break rather than now of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I had thought they would be received as a bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: We're happy to do that. The only thing is they have been entered into the e-court system as separate documents, so if that's possible, but it may be administratively problematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will see whether we can get them as a bundle over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And three minutes, I would suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, my worry is that the tape is going to run out at any moment, Mr. Smith. Keep trying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, also did you provide some -- did your office provide some photographs to the Tribunal of some of the missing people or of some of the individuals named in Annex A to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct. The files we submitted to the Tribunal included photographs of missing persons whenever we had those in our possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I seek to tender these six photographs. They're in the index from 241 to 247, index number. And just for information, the missing person questionnaires was from 1 to 238. Again, that might be something that needs to be done at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: These, too, will be dealt with after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Mr. Grujic, is it the case that there is a small group of questionnaires, perhaps under about 20, that haven't been forwarded to the Office of the Prosecutor and you will attempt to forward them in the next -- in the coming days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct. They weren't forwarded because the questionnaires were originally forwarded as early as 1995. Some were only produced later, and it was impossible to ascertain in relation to some that they were in relation to persons for whom questionnaires were requested. There are questionnaires missing in relation to two persons, Ruzica Markobasic and Stanoje Cupic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I can just turn you to tab 2.11, please. And this is ERN number 0600-3793 entitled list of remains exhumed at Novo Groblje in Vukovar, who, according to documentation received from Serbia and Montenegro were found in graves at Velepromet. Mr. Grujic, this list contains 15 names of people who were exhumed at the new cemetery in Vukovar and have been identified by the Serb authorities that they were originally found in a grave in Velepromet, or near Velepromet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And if we look at the second page of that document, which is 0600-3794, do we see here a note that was found on a number of the bodies that have been identified in this list, when they were exhumed at the Vukovar new cemetery stating that this body was located by the railway opposite Velepromet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And about how many of the bodies that were exhumed at the Vukovar new cemetery had that particular note on them, of the 15?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Four bodies had the same kind of document on it, which indicates that all four bodies came from the same grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: But in any event, you were notified by the Serb authorities that these 15 bodies were, in fact, retrieved from a grave at the rear of Velepromet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: They were not the ones who notify us. It was found in the documents that they had submitted to us. This documentation included the original document which you have just referred to about this grave being found containing 19 marked bodies. We found such bodies with lists at the Vukovar cemetery, and there were documents in their pockets, and official documents were later drawn up about all of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And just the one last question. If we turn to tab 2.12, please. This is ERN 0600-3703, "Locations in Serbia from where the mortal remains of victims from Vukovar were retrieved." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This map shows where victims were buried in what was then the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The map also indicates the places where we took over the remains of those victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I seek to tender that map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It, too, will be received after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are tendering 2.11?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: 2.11. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It, too, will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have finished my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will comment after the break, because of the tape. We will now adjourn for 20 minutes. At 10 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Court Officer.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a quick correction for the transcript and the record. The document at tab 3.5 has been assigned exhibit number 551. The document at tab 2.11 will be Exhibit 552. And the document at tab 2.12 will become Exhibit 553. Further, all the questionnaires with the reference number from index 1 to 238 will become Exhibit 554. While the six photographs with index number 241 to 247 will become Exhibit 555. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, indeed. Mr. Smith, we would point out that the original estimate for this witness was some four hours. Yesterday the need for speed to try and ensure that he could be free by tomorrow when we adjourn was identified. The important evidence for the most part came in those last rushed half hour or so of the second period. And most of the first period was essentially a repetition of what is already in the report. If we could point out that the result was that we have not achieved the sort of speed that had been hoped for in dealing with the important parts of the evidence. There is no need for you to comment, just drawing to your attention that it has fallen short of what we had expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I am attorney-at-law, Miroslav Vasic, one of Mr. Mrksic's defence counsel. Before we begin, could I just please draw your attention to one thing. Make a short pause after each of my questions since we speak the same language, to make the interpretation possible.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: By all means, I'll try to keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the start of your examination-in-chief we heard about your CV, we heard about your qualifications. I would just like to ask you something in relation to the specialised courses that you took. You say that you competed a one-year specialised course in state security. Did you not, in fact, work for state security since 1984; more precisely, in its Osijek department or outpost?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No. To be quite specific, it was since 1972 that I had been working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So from 1972 to 1990, that is the period that you had been working for the State Security Service. Were you staying in Osijek all this time?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No, not 1992. Yes, April 1992. That's right. From 1972 to 1992. And I spent this entire period in the State Security Service. That's what it was called. It was later renamed Service for the Protection of the Constitutional Order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You say you were a specialist for intelligence and counter-intelligence activities. But you also dealt with terrorism and uncovering terrorist activity in your area, right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. For a while, and I think that's reflected in my CV, while I was working with the service I started at the grass roots level, if you like, and I rose all the way up. I spent a certain period of time dealing with anti-terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You specified at one point that your service changed its name and was now called the Service for the Protection of the Constitutional Order. When was this exactly?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I think this occurred sometime in 1996, possibly 1997, but I'm not quite certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: There is something that I saw, and please correct me if I'm wrong, in 1990 you became head of the wartime section office of the Security Service in Osijek, right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is indeed what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when this wartime section office was set up of which you were head?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't tell you. I'm not authorised to tell you that, and this is not the subject of my evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: But we can agree that back in 1990 there was no war in the former Yugoslavia, was there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Was that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can we agree on the fact that back in 1990 there was no war in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: There was no war, but the situation was such that the tensions were high and there were sporadic incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there another section office like this in Vukovar, or did your own office perhaps set one up?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I should clarify a thing or two about these wartime section offices. These were conceived and came into existence from the time this service was created. From the time I first came there, these section offices were set up. They were set up for the eventuality of clashes or war. They were supposed to start operating in these areas, and this was merely a way to organise civilians in a given area. My area only had to do with the town of Osijek.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So there was a special section office in Vukovar, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time you submitted reports to the headquarters at the Ministry of the Interior in Zagreb, right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When the wartime section office was set up, did the nature of your assignments change in relation to your peacetime activities prior to 1990?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In 1990 and 1991, apart from the tasks given to you through the regular chain from the minister of the interior, did your service also receive orders from Branimir Glavas in Osijek?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No. No, the part that I worked in certainly did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us: In view of the fact that you worked on terrorism and discovering terrorist groups in the -- in late 1990 and early 1991, was a terrorist group discovered in your area, the victims of which were ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of any such thing, but certainly certain groups were discovered which could be linked to terrorism. I personally discovered one such group, and it was dealt with in the courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether in the course of your professional work in the period we are now talking about, that is 1991, did you discover the -- about the operations of a terrorist group headed by Franjo Kracak in Eastern Slavonia? Do you have such information?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your office covered a border area of the Republic of Croatia in the direction of Hungary. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No. It covered the town of Osijek and the then Osijek municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In late 1990, in the course of your operative work, did you come by information about the organising and arming of HDZ members in Osijek conducted by Branimir Glavas?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I arrived at such information that the HDZ was arming, also that the surrounding villages and their inhabitants were being armed by the JNA. I personally participated in some contacts, and this is well documented, aiming at listing these weapons and possibly handing them over.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you participated in listing and handing over weapons; you're referring to the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some of these wanted to hand over their weapons voluntarily, which they had received from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Within in your service, was the same kind of activity organised with respect to the weapons handed out by the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, wherever possible. Yes. As I said, they handed over weapons voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. In the first half of 1991, within the scope of your professional activities, were you aware of the planting of explosives in catering establishments owned by ethnic Serbs and frequent night-time attacks on the homes of Serb citizens in Osijek?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This did not fall within the purview of my work, but wherever there were elements indicating terrorist activity, we delivered such information to our superior services, which was then the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. You say this was something done by the public security service. This means that such incidents were described as ordinary attacks on life, limb or security of citizens, not as organised activity. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, in some cases, yes; in some cases, no. For example, the explosion at the political -- at Politika office was placed within the context of a terrorist attack and was investigated as such, and I participated in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I misunderstood your previous reply. It's clear to me now. At that time did you receive any reports from the public security service about the disappearances of citizens of Serb ethnicity? And if you did, did this indicate that there might be organised attacks on a particular population?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: As I said, missing persons fall within the purview of the public security. They have a missing persons service. They did then and they do now. And it was they who dealt with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that in connection with arming in the area where you conducted your professional duties you had certain tasks. I would like to know whether in this period of discovering the distribution of weapons in the area, regardless of whether these were handed out by the HDZ or whether this was happening in the surrounding villages, as you said, whether you contacted the JNA security administration or the security organs working on suppressing the smuggling of weapons into the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: In 1990, yes. I worked on one particular case, together with members of that service.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You remained the head of this war section office throughout the critical period in Eastern Slavonia in 1990 and 1991, and you followed the pre-war and wartime events from there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As part of the work you carried out, I assume you were familiar with the work of these commissions which were established in 1991 by the government of the Republic of Croatia dealing with the protection of detained persons and searching for missing persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No, not really. I didn't have contacts with that commission. It did its job and had it deemed it necessary, it would probably have contacted us an the ground. But I have no knowledge that they ever did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: As part of your work, did you learn at the time how exchanges were conducted in late 1991 and by whom?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did have some knowledge about that. These were exchanges carried out, one might say, on the local level. I know in particular that there was an exchange when, and that was still in 1990, when a bus load of civilians was taken prisoner in Markusica by members of the milicija, and they were held in Markusica and Sodolvci. And the head of operations or, I don't know, the head of the public security service had direct contacts with representatives of the JNA and representatives of those paramilitary formations in Markusica, and that was when the exchange was carried out. And this was the pattern. Contact was made with those in charge at the local level, and those exchanges were carried out. The data from these exchanges were later incorporated into our information based on the lists kept at the time, or the police records, which were made at the place of exchange or the place of release. It wasn't always an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, there is information dating from that period in 1991 concerning those exchanges, and this information was transferred to your commission when it was established in 1993. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. All the information that we could gain from that period is now in our administration. Frequently, when people applied to us in order to prove that they are entitled to the status of a prisoner - and they were not recorded at the time because the commission was established only in late 1991 and there had been exchanges previously - we then asked through official channels that the police and other bodies deliver to us document on the basis of which an administrative procedure can be initiated and the status proved. To sum up, the information you asked about, as far as is possible, is available in our administration and is one of the bases for the information that I have presented in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume that in the archives of your commission there is also information about an exchange which took place in December 1991 where 44 prisoners from Vukovar, together with Dr. Vesna Bosanac and Dr. Njavro, were exchanged for JNA officers who belonged to the so-called Labrador group which was established by the security administration. Was that information available to you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I do have information that that exchange took place. I know that for certain. We have a list of the people who were exchanged, and these persons who were exchanged have been incorporated in this figure of 7.666.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As part of the work that you did in the Security Service, you will have had information about the activities of the Labrador group, and their discovery and arrest; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: No, but I believe they had information about me. That was their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the network of collaborators of this group went to the very top of the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that, but I happen to know the man who was in charge of that group, Mr. Trazivuk, because he was at the head of the administration and he was my chief. I know him, but I did not know about the Labrador group until it was discovered by others. I was not that well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: After this group was discovered on the 15th of September, 1991, did you here have any tasks on discovering the network of their associates in the town of Osijek?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's one of the fundamentals of the counter-intelligence service. That's why it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that this operation of discovering the network of collaborators was suddenly interrupted and that it was never fully uncovered in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's something one can discuss from various standpoints, but I would not agree with the way you have put it. I'm absolutely sure, and I know that there was intensive work on this, not just in the case of the Labrador group, but also other services. Not just the Security Service, the JNA and internally. But the fundamental goal of the counter-intelligence service is to collect any information indicating that any foreign service is taking offensive action against the state. I could not agree with you categorically. I can say that I'm sure that work on this continued, but the question is how much one was able to prove and how much was proved. And, as I say, I was not involved in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You probably know that Mr. Aleksandar Vasiljevic was personally involved in this exchange at Pleso airport in Zagreb. Can you tell us who was there from the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware why the commissioner of the Vukovar municipality was not exchanged in this group? Was there any special reason?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I cannot speak about something I did not participate in or about which I do not have documents. I can talk about facts. And with respect to that group, as I said, I have documents showing that the group was released. Who it was that selected on both sides and how this was done is a completely different question. I know that when I started doing this job I insisted and managed to achieve the exchange and release of all for whom I had information. I never agreed to partial exchanges because those were a threat to those who would remain in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The commission established in late 1991, or the commissions, did they function according to the same principle you have just mentioned when negotiating exchanges?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: As I said, I can tell you what the organisation was like, but I cannot tell you what the criteria used by others were. This commission, from various sources, learnt that a certain number of people had been imprisoned. In order to achieve their release, they had to agree to a meeting with those who were able to release those people. After scheduling a meeting, negotiations began on releasing the particular group or population in question. What mechanisms were involved there, I cannot say. It's a fact that this was the way things happened. Usually representatives of the international community participated in those negotiations. When I was doing this, they always did because I refused to work without them. But it was all a matter of the current assessment of the situation, the current possibilities, the negotiations, and I really cannot say why someone selected someone by name to take part in an exchange, either on one side or the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic. I have one more question. I think my time is running out. Could you tell us if you know who was at the head of these commissions in 1991 and under whose auspices they were established and to whom they were responsible for their work?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: They were established within the Ministry of Defence. So, in a manner of speaking, they were under the auspices of the Ministry of Defence, which provided their logistical support. I really cannot tell you who the people were; they came and went at the head of these commissions. And it was precisely for this reason that the government decided to establish its own commission, which would have a better insight into the situation and better possibilities for solving this very important humanitarian issue. Not just for Croatia, but for the entire territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: This commission reported to the government, to the cabinet, am I right? Your commission, I mean.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: My commission reported exclusively to the government, that is the cabinet, as does the present commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. We will adjourn now and we will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning. I'm sure counsel will remain conscious of the need to concentrate on what is relevant.
